meta.title: Pricing — Free to Send, Drive from $2.49
meta.ogTitle: BIShare Pricing — Free to Send, Drive from $2.49

description: Sending is free: unlimited device-to-device transfers, encrypted links up to 100 GB, no account, no ads. BIShare Drive storage: 5 GB free, plans from $2.49 a month.
heading: Sending is free. All of it.

included.network: Unlimited transfers between nearby devices — no size cap at all
included.e2e: End-to-end encrypted on every path, including links
included.links: Encrypted share links up to 100 GB, with QR and 6-character codes
included.expire: Links auto-expire after 6, 12 or 24 hours; nothing is kept
included.rooms: Rooms — share with a group over one short code
included.platforms: iOS, Android, macOS, Windows, and Linux
included.source: Open source under the Apache 2.0 licence — no ads, no tracking

ctaNote: Sending has no paid tier, and none is planned. Nothing here is a trial.

drive.title: BIShare Drive, if you want storage
drive.body: Optional end-to-end encrypted storage for your files and phone photos, in the BIShare apps and at drive.bishare.app. Sending stays free with or without it.
drive.note: Prices in US dollars; the App Store or Google Play shows the price in your currency. A year costs the same as ten months. Plans are bought in the BIShare app and can be cancelled at any time.

compare.title: What the alternatives charge
compare.note: Competitor prices are their published list prices and change over time; check their sites for current figures.

why.a: Because it costs us almost nothing to run. Nearby transfers go straight between your devices and never touch a server, so the expensive part of file sharing simply does not happen. Links stream through storage in chunks and delete themselves after 6, 12 or 24 hours, which keeps that side to pennies. The size caps other services impose are pricing decisions, not physics — and BIShare is open source, so you can read the code that proves it.

catch.a: There is no catch, and that is checkable rather than a promise: the source is public under Apache 2.0, there are no ads, no tracking, and no account to create to send — so there is no profile to sell. Files sent over your own network never reach us at all, and files sent by link are encrypted before they leave your device, so we hold bytes we cannot read.

limits.a: Transfers between devices on the same network have no size limit — the ceiling is the receiving device's free space. Share links carry up to 100 GB per transfer and expire after 6, 12 or 24 hours. Both are free, with no account on either end.

later.a: Sending stays free, and no paid tier for it is planned. The one paid service is BIShare Drive, optional encrypted storage with 5 GB free and paid plans for more: something new alongside sending, not a wall placed around what already works. And because the project is licensed under Apache 2.0, the version you have today stays free regardless.
